q: After abdominal trauma, what is the answer, and what do you assume when there is pain?
a: surgery; bleeding and leaking — go
surgery; assume bleed and leak; go
surgery is the answer; assume something bleeding and leaking
surgery; pain = bleed + leak; go
why: Surgery is the answer. Pain after trauma: assume something is bleeding and something is leaking. Go.

q: About how many liters of blood does the body have, and how much can the abdomen hide before it looks swollen or bruised?
a: about 6 L; a couple of 2-liter bottles
6 liters; couple of 2L bottles
about 6; couple of 2-liter bottles before swollen/bruised
6 L body; abdomen holds couple of 2L bottles
why: About 6 liters in the body. The abdomen can hold a couple of 2-liter bottles before it looks swollen or bruised. Do not wait for a fat, bruised belly.

q: Breath sounds are fine and you still have unexplained shock. Where do you think the bleed is?
a: abdomen
the abdomen
belly / abdomen
assume abdomen
why: Good lungs + shock you cannot explain = think abdomen. Chest bleed would change breath sounds.

q: Right after a wreck, will you see fever yet if a hollow organ just leaked?
a: no
no fever yet
no — infection takes time
not yet
why: Right after the wreck you will not see fever even if a hollow organ leaked. Infection takes time.

q: Which organs live in the right upper and left upper?
a: right upper liver+gallbladder; left upper stomach+spleen
RUQ liver and gallbladder; LUQ stomach and spleen
right upper: liver and gallbladder; left upper: stomach and spleen
liver+gallbladder right upper; stomach+spleen left upper
why: Right upper = liver (solid) and gallbladder (hollow). Left upper = stomach (hollow) and spleen (solid).

q: Where do appendix and kidneys live on the map?
a: appendix right lower; kidneys flank/back
appendix = right lower; kidneys = flank / back
RLQ appendix; flank kidneys
appendix right lower; kidneys not a front-quadrant organ — flank
why: Appendix = right lower. Kidneys = flank / back. Not a front-quadrant organ.

q: Solid organs do what? Hollow organs do what? Early on scene can you tell them apart?
a: solid bleed; hollow leak; no — early feel the same
solid bleed (hemorrhagic); hollow leak (peritonitis/septic later); cannot sort on scene
bleed vs leak; early same — transport
solid bleed; hollow spill/irritate lining; early same — go
why: Solid bleed. Hollow leak (peritonitis / septic later). Early leak and early bleed feel the same. Transport.

q: Why can one hit smash liver and spleen in a kid?
a: organs bigger, closer, more exposed under short rib cage
kid organs bigger/closer/more exposed
packed closer and short rib cage leaves them more exposed
bigger for the belly, closer, short ribs — one hit both
why: Kid organs are bigger for the belly, packed closer, and the short rib cage leaves them more exposed. One hit can smash liver and spleen at once.

q: Biggest bleeder organ, and where can its pain refer?
a: liver; right shoulder
liver — biggest bleeder; right shoulder
liver (right ribs); pain to right shoulder
liver; right shoulder same path as gallbladder
why: Liver is the biggest bleeder. Right lower ribs can cut it. Pain can go to the right shoulder (same path as gallbladder).

q: Bowel sounds / gurgles in the chest after trauma mean what?
a: torn diaphragm — bowel in the chest
diaphragm tear; bowel into chest
torn diaphragm
diaphragm tear lets bowel into the chest
why: Diaphragm tear lets bowel into the chest. Hard to breathe. Gurgles when you listen on the chest.

q: Cullen’s sign is a bruise where, and do you wait for it?
a: around the belly button; no do not wait
belly button; late — do not wait
bruise around belly button; do not wait
belly-button bruise; late — go anyway
why: Cullen’s sign: bruise around the belly button = a lot of blood already inside. Late. Do not wait for it.

q: Where should the seatbelt catch, and how do you transport second-half pregnancy?
a: pelvis not soft belly; left side
belt on pelvis; second half left side
pelvis (booster for kids); left side — supine hypotensive if flat
catch pelvis; second-half pregnancy left side
why: Belt catches the pelvis, not the soft belly. Second half of pregnancy: left side. Flat lets the uterus sandwich aorta and vena cava (supine hypotensive syndrome).

q: Evisceration: push organs back? Dressing order?
a: do not push; moist then plastic for heat
no push; moist sterile then plastic
do not push back; moist on organs, plastic over for heat
no push; moist then plastic (wet/bulky dry/blankets if no plastic)
why: Do not push organs back in. Moist sterile on the organs, plastic over that for heat. No big plastic: wet, then bulky dry, then blankets.

q: High belly wound vs low belly wound — which dressing?
a: high: plastic/occlusive like chest; low: dry sterile
high belly plastic; low belly dry sterile
could be chest → plastic; lower no chest concern → dry sterile
high lean plastic; low dry sterile
why: High belly that could be chest → plastic / occlusive. Lower belly, no chest concern → dry sterile.

q: XABCs vs board, and which quadrant do you palpate last?
a: XABCs first board later; sore / hurt quadrant last
XABCs first, Platinum 10, board after; sore last
life threats first board later; palpate sore last
XABCs first; hurt quadrant LAST
why: XABCs first. Board after life threats. Platinum 10. Look first. Push four quadrants. Hurt quadrant LAST.

q: Pulsating abdominal mass means what until proven otherwise?
a: abdominal aortic aneurysm
AAA / abdominal aortic aneurysm
abdominal aortic aneurysm until proven otherwise
AAA
why: Pulsating mass = abdominal aortic aneurysm until proven otherwise. Not a normal pulse-check spot.

q: Flank always points to which organ? Gray Turner bruise means blood where?
a: kidney; back compartment
kidney; blood in the back compartment
flank = kidney; Gray Turner = back-compartment blood
kidney; Gray Turner flank bruise = back compartment
why: Flank = kidney. Always. Gray Turner: bruise on the flank. Blood in the back compartment. Late.

q: Bad pelvis break can dump how much blood, and what three life threats?
a: 2+ L of ~6 (a third); bone bleed, femoral vessel cut, poke bladder/rectum
2+ liters / third of tank; bone, femoral artery/vein, bladder or rectum
2+ of about 6; bone bleed + femoral cut + poke hollow organs
2+ liters; bone bleed, femoral vessel, poke bladder/rectum infection
why: Worst bone for bleeding. 2+ liters of about 6 — a third. Three threats: bone bleed, femoral artery or vein cut, poke bladder or rectum → infection later.

q: Where can you pack hemostatic gauze, and can you pack deep belly or chest?
a: junctions only — groin and just inside shoulder; no deep belly/chest
groin and inside shoulder junctions; cannot pack deep belly or chest
junctions groin/inside shoulder only; surgery for deep belly/chest
only junctions; cannot pack deep belly or chest
why: Pack hemostatic gauze only at junctions — groin and just inside the shoulder. You cannot pack a deep belly or a chest. Surgery.

q: Genital bleed vs not bleeding — which dressing? Vaginal bleed: pack or pad?
a: blood → dry sterile; no blood → moist; pad outside do not pack
any bleed dry; not bleeding moist (eyes/guts list); vaginal pad outside save pads
dry if blood, moist if no blood; pad outside never pack vagina
bleed dry sterile; no bleed moist sterile; pad outside, save pads
why: Any bleed gets dry sterile. Not bleeding: moist sterile (same list as eyes and guts). Vaginal bleed: pad outside. Do not pack. Save the pads.

q: Pregnant trauma: why treat shock early, and Narcan — who decides?
a: mom looks fine longer; call medical control — do not decide Narcan yourself
higher volume mom looks fine; fetus already in trouble; call med control for Narcan
treat shock early — mom looks fine longer; bag her / call medical control for Narcan
mom fine longer while baby in trouble; call doctor — you can bag her
why: Higher pregnant blood volume — mom looks fine longer. Treat shock early. If opioids whole pregnancy, fetus may be dependent. You can bag her. Call medical control. Do not decide Narcan yourself.

q: Sexual assault evidence: paper or plastic bag? Why?
a: paper bag; plastic traps moisture and ruins DNA
paper; plastic ruins DNA
clothes/evidence in paper bag — plastic traps moisture
paper bag not plastic
why: Clothes and evidence go in a paper bag. Plastic traps moisture and ruins DNA.

q: Kehr sign is pain to the shoulder. Class Right upper maps to which shoulder/organs? Book classic often which side from spleen?
a: right shoulder gallbladder/liver; book often left shoulder spleen
class Right upper → right shoulder (gallbladder/liver); book classic left shoulder spleen
right shoulder liver/gallbladder; left shoulder smashed spleen
RUQ→right shoulder; book often left from spleen
why: Kehr = pain to the shoulder. Class used Right upper → right shoulder (gallbladder / liver). Book classic is often left shoulder from a smashed spleen.

q: Cold trauma/shock patient — can they clot? What do you do?
a: no — cold cannot clot; keep them warm
cold blood does not clot; keep warm
cannot clot when cold; keep every trauma/shock patient warm
no clot if cold; keep warm
why: Cold patients cannot clot. Keep every trauma / shock patient warm. Cold blood does not clot.
